model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the average annual growth rates in percent for four key economic indicators—World GDP (Welt-BIP), World Trade (Welthandel), German Exports (Exporte Deutschland), and German Industrial Production (Industrieproduktion Deutschland)—across three decades: the 2000s, 2010s, and 2020s. The vertical axis ranges from -2.0% to 6.0%, with increments of 1.0%, while the horizontal axis categorizes the data by decade. In the 2000s, World GDP grew at 3.9%, World Trade at 5.4%, German Exports at 5.3%, and German Industrial Production at 1.0%. In the 2010s, growth rates declined slightly: World GDP at 3.7%, World Trade at 4.8%, German Exports at 5.0%, and German Industrial Production at 2.2%. By the 2020s, growth slowed further: World GDP at 2.7%, World Trade at 2.3%, German Exports at 0.4%, and German Industrial Production fell to -1.5%, the only negative value in the chart. The bars are color-coded and grouped by decade, with green for World GDP, light green for World Trade, blue for German Exports, and light blue for German Industrial Production. The chart visually highlights a general deceleration in growth across all indicators over time, with German Industrial Production experiencing a notable contraction in the 2020s.
